_comment: EXT-63, arm 28b — ATTRIBUTION PAIR for LV-1's surviving actuator.  1 h,
LV-4 + LV-5 armed, LV-2 de-mean DELIBERATELY OFF, LV-1 OFF.
WHY.  Arm 27 falsified the inertness prediction: with the frame gate retired by LV-4,
LV-1 still moved the level by ~10 TECU (first 58 ep: LV-1 ON mean 38.80, OFF 28.70,
difference flat at -9..-12 from epoch 10 on).  So a second actuator exists, and the
algebra points at LV-2 itself:
the de-meaned fold asserts  dx_i = innov_i - mu  with  mu = sum(lam*innov)/sum(lam)
and  innov_i = value_abs_i - x_lin_i,  so  mu = mean(value_abs) - mean(x_lin)
and the target is   x_abs_i = value_abs_i - mean(value_abs) + mean(x_lin).
The common-mode component of that target is mean(x_lin) -- the mean of the FROZEN
first-epoch code-bias seeds.  The carry still puts sum(lam) ~ 100 information units on
the common mode (the de-mean changes the RHS, never the information), so it PINS the
receiver-DCB common mode to the seed frame.  LV-1 changes exactly that frame: the
reframed iono seed feeds initializeCodeBiases, which derives x_lin(cb) by subtracting
the seeded iono.
PREDICTION, STATED BEFORE THE RUN: with LV-2 OFF, arms 28a and 28b agree (no
systematic level difference) -- because the un-demeaned fold asserts x_abs = value_abs
outright, which is frame-free, so LV-1 loses its last channel.  If they still differ,
the actuator is somewhere else again and neither the gate nor the de-mean explains it.
NOTE what this pair does NOT claim: with LV-2 off and LV-4 admitting the full carry,
the common mode is owned by the carry's own memory.  Expect a poor level in BOTH arms.
The comparison is arm-to-arm, not against GIM.
